question: Tardieu spots (subpleural and subpericardial petechial haemorrhages) are pathognomonic of asphyxia and confirm the diagnosis when present.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Tardieu spots are suggestive, not pathognomonic. They occur in non-asphyxial deaths (raised venous pressure states) and may be absent in genuine asphyxial deaths. Always interpret in clinical context with all PM findings.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is FALSE. Tardieu spots are a sign of asphyxia, not proof of it. They appear in any death associated with raised venous pressure (e.g., right heart failure, sepsis) and are absent in up to 30% of asphyxial deaths. No single PM sign confirms asphyxia; the diagnosis requires integration of all findings.
